blocs.name: NATO
blocs.text: Military alliance in which an attack on one member counts as an attack on all (Article 5). Finland joined in 2023 and Sweden in 2024, after Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

blocs.name: EU
blocs.text: Political and economic union with a single market. 21 members use the euro; Bulgaria adopted it in January 2026.

blocs.name: ASEAN
blocs.text: Regional group that decides by consensus and avoids interfering in members' internal affairs. Timor-Leste became the 11th member in October 2025.

blocs.name: BRICS
blocs.text: Group of large emerging economies. Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran and the UAE joined in 2024 and Indonesia in 2025; Saudi Arabia was invited but has not confirmed.

blocs.name: SCO
blocs.text: Security and economic group led by China and Russia. Iran joined in 2023 and Belarus in 2024.

blocs.name: CSTO
blocs.text: Russia-led military alliance of former Soviet states.

blocs.name: G7
blocs.text: Yearly summit of seven large advanced economies; the EU also takes part.

blocs.name: Quad
blocs.text: Security talks between the US, Japan, India and Australia, focused on the Indo-Pacific.

blocs.name: AUKUS
blocs.text: Pact under which the US and UK are helping Australia acquire nuclear-powered submarines.

blocs.name: GCC
blocs.text: Political and economic union of six Gulf monarchies.

blocs.name: OPEC
blocs.full: Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries
blocs.text: Group of 11 oil exporters that sets production targets, together with Russia and others as OPEC+. Angola left in 2024 and the UAE in May 2026.

blocs.name: AES
blocs.label: Sahel alliance (AES)
blocs.text: Confederation of three military-run states that left ECOWAS, effective January 2025.
